ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: SESOI=.27 is the largest observed effect, not smallest — must cross-reference with reported effect sizes
ground_truth.original_snippet: with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .11.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .27.
ground_truth.description: Changed SESOI from .11 to .27 (the LARGEST observed effect, not smallest) — makes equivalence tests trivially easy; biases toward confirming moral incongruence is unique to pornography

matched_finding.subcategory: SESOI selection and equivalence bound justification
matched_finding.description: The equivalence bound (δ = |.11|) is derived from the smallest effect observed in prior pornography studies using a different moderator (religiousness rather than moral disapproval directly) and a less validated outcome measure. The authors acknowledge this is 'extremely conservative' but justify it as serving the purpose of demonstrating uniqueness. However, using an extremely conservative equivalence bound makes it very easy to fail to demonstrate equivalence with zero (i.e., easy to find non-null effects for gambling/substances), which would actually disconfirm their hypotheses. Conversely, if the bound is too small, it may be nearly impossible to achieve equivalence even for truly negligible effects. The SESOI should be justified on substantive grounds (what effect size would be practically meaningful) rather than selected to serve the narrative goal.
matched_finding.quote: Collectively, then, setting our equivalence region to δ= |.11| represents an extremely conservative analytic decision. However, as a primary purpose of the present work is to evaluate whether moral incongruence is unique in its contribution to self-reports of pornography addiction, in contrast to other addictions, we elected to use an especially small SESOI for our analyses.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Items on different scales averaged without standardizing — must notice 0-5 vs 0/3/6 scales
ground_truth.original_snippet: Responses to each of the above five items will be standardized, and an average will be taken for each substance of interest
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest
ground_truth.description: Removed standardization before averaging — items use different scales (0-5 vs 0/3/6); raw averaging lets larger-scale items dominate composite, creating measurement artifact

matched_finding.subcategory: averaging items with different response scales
matched_finding.description: The NIDA-ASSIST composite score is computed by averaging five items, but three items use a 0-5 frequency scale while two items use a 0/3/6 scale (No, Never / Yes, but not in past 3 months / Yes, in past 3 months). Averaging items with different response scales and different ranges produces a composite with unclear psychometric meaning. The 0/3/6 items have a maximum of 6 while the frequency items have a maximum of 5, meaning the two dichotomous-style items will have disproportionate influence on the composite. This is a basic measurement error that should be corrected by standardizing items before averaging or using a different aggregation approach.
matched_finding.quote: Participants will also respond to two questions 'Has a friend or relative or anyone else ever expressed concern about your use of or engagement in the following?' and 'Have you ever tried and failed to control, cut down or stop using or engaging in the following?' for each substance on 3 point scale (0 = No, Never; 3 = Yes, but not in the past 3 months; and 6 = Yes, In the past 3 months). Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: 'Severity of consequences' conflates moral incongruence with genuine addiction — must understand the construct definition
ground_truth.original_snippet: Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of a behavior with frequency of engaging in the action.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of a behavior with severity of consequences from the action.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'frequency of engaging' to 'severity of consequences' — transforms moral incongruence (behavior-value mismatch) into moralized distress about real problems, conflating it with the alternative explanation

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: 'Limits temporal ordering' is weaker than 'precludes causal inference' — must know the distinction matters
ground_truth.original_snippet: This sample is cross-sectional, precluding causal inference.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: This sample is cross-sectional, which limits the temporal ordering of variables.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'precluding causal inference' to 'limits temporal ordering' — leaves room for causal interpretation when cross-sectional data fundamentally cannot establish causation

matched_finding.description: The study is entirely cross-sectional, yet the authors make causal-sounding claims throughout (e.g., moral incongruence 'predicts' or 'drives' feelings of addiction, moral disapproval 'amplifies' links). Cross-sectional moderation analyses cannot establish temporal precedence or causality. The direction of effects is entirely ambiguous: people who feel addicted to pornography may retrospectively report greater moral disapproval, or a third variable may cause both. While the authors mention this limitation briefly, they do not adequately constrain their causal language throughout the manuscript.
matched_finding.quote: moral disapproval of pornography likely amplifies the links between pornography use and self-reported feelings of compulsivity or addiction

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Says 8 analyses but earlier lists 10 corresponding to 8 behaviors + 2 parallel measures — countable
ground_truth.original_snippet: In total, we will conduct 10 moderation analyses for moral disapproval and frequency, corresponding to the 8 target behaviors/variables of interest, with pornography and gambling repeated for both the NIDA-ASSIST measure and the validate measures of problematic use (the Brief Pornography Screen and ...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In total, we will conduct 8 moderation analyses for moral disapproval and frequency, corresponding to the 8 target behaviors/variables of interest, with pornography and gambling assessed using the validate measures of problematic use (the Brief Pornography Screen and the Problem Gambling Severity In...
ground_truth.description: Changed from 10 to 8 analyses, removing parallel NIDA-ASSIST analyses for pornography/gambling — eliminates the measurement-equivalence check essential for fair cross-behavior comparison

matched_finding.description: Pornography and gambling are assessed using validated, domain-specific scales (Brief Pornography Screen and Problem Gambling Severity Index) in addition to the modified NIDA-ASSIST items, while all substance use outcomes rely solely on the modified NIDA-ASSIST. This creates a measurement asymmetry: pornography and gambling outcomes have better psychometric properties and more items, potentially yielding more reliable and valid scores. Differences in effect sizes across domains could reflect measurement quality differences rather than true differences in moral incongruence effects. The authors acknowledge this but do not adequately address it in their analytic plan.
matched_finding.quote: Although such an approach is not currently validated for gambling or pornography, given the inclusion of other validated scales to assess these outcomes (see below), including them within the NIDA-ASSIST will not decrement our ability to evaluate our key hypotheses.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: DWLS sensitivity analysis removed — must know OLS may fail for ordinal addiction measures
ground_truth.original_snippet: Similar to prior works (Grubbs, Lee, et al., 2020), should basic assumptions of regression be violated substantially, we will construct latent variable models using the lavaan package (Rosseel, 2012) for R Statistical Software, using diagonally weighted least squares estimation, as such an estimator...
ground_truth.description: Deleted entire planned DWLS latent variable sensitivity analysis — removes backup for when OLS assumptions fail (likely for ordinal/skewed addiction measures)

matched_finding.description: The primary analyses use OLS regression (via the lm function) with outcomes that are ordinal composites (averaged Likert-type items). While the authors note they will test regression assumptions and conduct supplemental analyses if violated, ordinal outcomes with limited response categories (especially the NIDA-ASSIST composite with only a few possible values) may systematically violate normality and homoscedasticity assumptions. For small subsamples (e.g., prescription drug misuse, n≈140), these violations could be severe. Ordinal regression or other appropriate methods should be the primary approach, not a supplemental one.
matched_finding.quote: Although Ordinary Least Squares techniques (such as the moderation analyses conducted by the Interactive application) in large sample sizes are often robust against some violations (Schmidt & Finan, 2018), in cases where assumptions are substantially violated, we will conduct supplemental analyses to test the robustness of our models

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Only age/gender matching — must know moral attitudes vary by race, income, region
ground_truth.original_snippet: the target sample size will be 2,500 American adults that match nationally representative norms for age, gender, census region, race/ethnicity, and income.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: the target sample size will be 2,500 American adults that match nationally representative norms for age and gender.
ground_truth.description: Removed census region, race/ethnicity, and income from quota-matching — dramatically weakens representativeness; these variables correlate with moral attitudes and substance use

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Moderator/predictor roles swapped — must know statistical symmetry ≠ conceptual symmetry
ground_truth.original_snippet: In this revised definition, moral disapproval moderates links between use and self-reported feelings of addiction, and it is this moderation that represents moral incongruence.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In this revised definition, use frequency moderates links between moral disapproval and self-reported feelings of addiction, and it is this moderation that represents moral incongruence.
ground_truth.description: Swapped moderator and focal predictor — though statistically symmetric, conceptually different: PPMI says disapproval changes the use-addiction link, not that use changes the disapproval-addiction link

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Raw variables in moderation — must know centering affects interaction interpretability
ground_truth.original_snippet: For moderation analyses, key variables will be centered (focal predictor and moderator) during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: For moderation analyses, key variables will be entered in their raw form during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.
ground_truth.description: Removed centering — main effects evaluated at raw zero (outside scale range for 1-7 disapproval scale); inflates multicollinearity with interaction term

matched_finding.subcategory: inconsistency in centering and interaction computation
matched_finding.description: The authors state that 'focal predictors (behavioral frequency measures) and moderators (moral disapproval questions) will be centered and their interaction term calculated' in SPSS, but then state 'For moderation analyses, key variables will be entered in their raw form during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.' These two statements are contradictory. If variables are centered before computing the product, the interaction term is the product of centered variables. If variables are entered in raw form and their product computed, the interaction term is not based on centered variables. This inconsistency could affect the interpretation of main effects in the moderation models.
matched_finding.quote: focal predictors (behavioral frequency measures) and moderators (moral disapproval questions) will be centered and their interaction term calculated... For moderation analyses, key variables will be entered in their raw form during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Non-users included — must understand floor effects make interaction meaningless
ground_truth.original_snippet: For each target behavior and corresponding measure of problematic use or addiction, key measures will be restricted to those who have engaged in the behavior within the past year. That is, we will only administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to participants who report engaging i...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: For each target behavior and corresponding measure of problematic use or addiction, key measures will be administered to all participants regardless of their engagement in the behavior. That is, we will administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to all participants in the sample.
ground_truth.description: Removed restriction to behavior-engagers — includes non-users who have zero frequency AND zero problems, creating massive floor effects that trivially inflate frequency-addiction correlations

matched_finding.subcategory: restriction of range in moral disapproval for substance users
matched_finding.description: The analyses are conducted among users of each substance/behavior. For substances like illicit drugs, users are likely to be a highly selected group with systematically different moral attitudes than non-users. Moral disapproval of illicit drug use among illicit drug users is likely to have severely restricted range (most users probably do not strongly morally disapprove of their own drug use, or they would not use). This restriction of range would attenuate the interaction effect, making it more likely to fall within the equivalence bounds—not because moral incongruence is truly absent, but because of a methodological artifact. This is not acknowledged.
matched_finding.quote: For each target behavior and corresponding measure of problematic use or addiction, key measures will be administered to all participants regardless of their engagement in the behavior.
